leftEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
leftEvidence.title: The wilderness generation becomes a present warning about rest

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: The psalm addresses present hearers: “Today, if you will hear his voice,” and warns against hardening hearts as at Meribah and Massah.
points.right: The argument says good news came to both generations, but the message did not profit those who were not united with faith.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: Forty years of grief ends with an oath that the generation will not enter the LORD’s rest.
points.right: God’s rest reaches back to creation, remains open through “today,” and is not exhausted by Joshua’s later entry.

payload.posture: Psalm 95 names the denied outcome as rest; Hebrews argues that Joshua’s entry did not exhaust the promise of rest.

rightEvidence.role: Refusal remembered as unbelief and lost rest
rightEvidence.title: Hebrews develops land-entry language into a remaining rest

payload.tension: The development expands the referent of rest without turning the original land crisis into a merely abstract idea.
payload.title: Land-entry failure and a rest that remains
